prompt_text: Who does backflow testing and repair near Liberty MO?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t look up live business listings, but here’s a quick, practical way to find qualified backflow testing and repair near Liberty, MO plus what to check before hiring:

Who to look for
- Local licensed plumbers (many perform backflow testing/repair).  
- Irrigation/waterworks companies that advertise backflow testing.  
- Fire protection/backflow specialists (for commercial systems).  
- The City of Liberty Public Works or your water utility—they often maintain a tester list or can tell you inspection requirements.

How to find them (search phrases to use)
- “backflow testing Liberty MO”  
- “backflow tester near Liberty MO”  
- “backflow repair Kansas City area” (Liberty is in the KC metro)  
Search on Google, Google Maps, Yelp, or the Yellow Pages.

What to verify before hiring
- Certification: Ask for the tester’s Missouri backflow prevention assembly tester certification (most cities require a certified tester).  
- Insurance and license: general plumbing license and liability insurance.  
- Experience with your device type (residential irrigation vs. commercial/fire line/testable assemblies).  
- Ask for references or recent clients.  
- Confirm they will file the test report with the City/utility if required.

Typical price range (approximate)
- Residential irrigation or simple assembly: roughly $60–$150 per device.  
- Commercial / complex assemblies or repairs: higher — depends on parts/labor. Get written estimates.

Sample questions to ask a company when you call
- “Are you certified to test backflow assemblies in Missouri?”  
- “Do you file the test report with the City of Liberty or the water utility?”  
- “How much do you charge for testing and what if the device needs repair?”  
- “Do you carry insurance and can you provide references?”

If you want, I can:
- Draft a short call/email script you can use to contact companies.  
- Help you craft a Google Maps search string and example review filters.  
- If you give me your ZIP code or whether this is residential or commercial, I’ll give more targeted guidance on likely companies to call. Which would you prefer?
